headline: ATX Bowers fall to 1-8 with 33.8 points left on bench
dek: A 84.16-point loss to The Dakstreet Boys came with 33.8 points on the bench, though even a perfect lineup would have fallen short.

sections.title: Your week
sections.md:
ATX Bowers lost 84.16 to 122.98 against The Dakstreet Boys and sit at **1-8**.

The best possible lineup was **117.96**, so the bench cost points but not this game. That lineup still loses by 5.02. You set **71%** of the available points.

- **MVP:** Drake Maye, **21.26** against our projection of 18.8.
- **Best surprise:** Jonah Coleman, **18.8** against our projection of 11.37.
- **Dud:** Ladd McConkey, **0.0** against our projection of 6.14.
- **Other misses:** Aaron Jones (**3.1**, our projection 12.48), Dalton Kincaid (**5.8**, 9.73) and Brenton Strange (**4.2**, 9.58). Mike Gesicki also scored **3.1**, and Rashee Rice scored **9.9**.

The bench stung most. Tank Dell scored **20.5** and Denzel Boston scored **15.8**. Dell for McConkey cost **20.5**, and Boston for Gesicki cost **12.7**. Jordan Addison for Strange was only **0.6**.

sections.title: Could you have known?
sections.md:
**Tank Dell over Ladd McConkey (20.5 points lost): variance.** Our projection preferred McConkey, 6.14 to 3.7. Dell's pregame usage was thin: **23%** snaps, **4%** target share, **2.8** xFP over the last three, in only one game. McConkey had a **10%** target share and **5.0** xFP. The one point for Dell was HOU's implied total of **23.0**, against **17.5** for LAC. That is not enough to start him, and a zero from McConkey was not predictable.

**Denzel Boston over Mike Gesicki (12.7 lost): our projection pointed the right way.** It had Boston at 10.56 and Gesicki at 7.88. Boston's usage backed that up:
- **90%** snaps
- **23%** target share
- **13.2** xFP over the last three

Gesicki's case was CIN's **27.8** implied total, but his xFP was only **6.6**. This one was a defensible call to make.

**Jordan Addison over Brenton Strange (0.6 lost): too close to call.** Our projection was 9.84 against 9.58, and the usage was comparable.

sections.title: Injuries on the field
sections.md:
- **Luther Burden III (CHI, Game of Throws):** concussion, diagnosed after a late fourth-quarter head-to-head hit. He had seven catches for 97 yards and a touchdown before leaving. Rome Odunze (The Dakstreet Boys) is next up and played **84%** of snaps. Chicago's Week 10 bye may give Burden time to clear protocol.
- **Rhamondre Stevenson (NE, Justiniscleann):** knee injury. He left in the third quarter and did not return, and the severity is not yet known. Lan Larison (**22%** snaps) is next up, and Corey Kiner is also named. His next chance to play is Nov. 15 against the Lions in Munich.
- **Xavier Worthy (KC, Bucky Charms):** hamstring. He was ruled out for the rest of the game and Andy Reid called him day-to-day. Your Rashee Rice played **58%** of snaps and is the next man up.
- **Justin Herbert (LAC, Bucky Charms):** left middle finger injury. He exited in the fourth quarter and did not return, and a fracture is possible. DJ Uiagalelei is next up.
- **Patrick Mahomes (KC, Lover Boys):** right elbow. He left in pain, came back and finished the game. His MRI was clean, though the elbow will be monitored this week. Justin Fields is the backup.
- **Jake Ferguson (DAL, Sebas350):** he took a hit to his left knee and was questionable to return. He played only **34%** of snaps, and Brevyn Spann-Ford (**70%**) is next up.
- **K.C. Concepcion (CLE, Just Win Baby):** non-contact ankle injury. He briefly left but returned and finished with four catches for 85 yards and a touchdown. Your Denzel Boston is the next man up if it flares up, and he played **93%** of snaps.
- **Jaylen Waddle (Sebas350):** he left with a concussion. Pat Bryant (Just Win Baby) scored the game-winning touchdown after that. If the Week 10 bye doesn't give Waddle enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

sections.title: Around the league
sections.md:
- **Chentudo El Venudo** had the high score, **167.48**, and beat Sebas350. They are **7-2**, and Kenneth Walker III led with 36.3.
- **Just Win Baby** beat I Love it Ra, 144.66 to 96.12, and lead the league at **8-1**.
- **Moore Than A Bite** edged Game of Throws, 143.44 to 139.18. Game of Throws would have won with a better lineup, since Alvin Kamara (7.9) sat while D'Andre Swift scored 3.1.
- **Bucky Charms** beat Lover Boys, 117.8 to 116.38, with a perfect 100% lineup. Lover Boys left Jordan Love (**36.18**) on the bench for J.K. Dobbins (3.2). They would have won with him.
- **Justiniscleann** beat SMA, 116.06 to 101.86, with C.J. Stroud (**36.36**) on the bench. They left 31.7 points there.
- **The Dakstreet Boys** are 2-7 after beating you.

sections.title: Grading last week's preview
sections.md:
Last week's one listed call was Jordan Addison over Dalton Kincaid. It missed narrowly: Addison scored **4.8** and Kincaid scored **5.8**.

The full suggested lineup scored **86.86**, against your actual **84.16**. That is 2.7 points more than you scored, and well short of the **117.96** best possible. The facts list only the Addison call, so I can't break down the rest of that lineup. The Dell and Boston decisions weren't part of that preview call.
